subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should #41484 be solved as narrow per-job/heartbeat elevated markers, or folded into broader Gateway-owned scheduling and execution provenance?
rationale: The code can support either shape, but choosing the trust boundary affects host-exec authorization, cron storage, heartbeat config, audit semantics, and upgrade compatibility.

options.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
options.body: Design one Gateway-owned provenance and authorization model for cron and heartbeat elevation, aligned with #71712 and the #96883 caller-scope work.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add focused cron and heartbeat elevated fields with explicit update/migration rules, accepting that broader scheduling provenance remains separate follow-up work.

options.title: Document Current Risk Temporarily
options.body: Keep current allowlist behavior while documenting the internal-source risk and wait for a larger scheduler security design.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
recommendation.body: Design one Gateway-owned provenance and authorization model for cron and heartbeat elevation, aligned with #71712 and the #96883 caller-scope work.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest merged cron security-boundary change and have current context on caller-scoped Gateway cron behavior.
